page_title: BBC Learning English - English at Work / Risky business
title: Risky business
description:
After accusing Anna of smoking in the office, Paul thinks the team needs an update on their health and safety policy. Find out the phrases you need to talk about being safe at work.
This episode focuses on the phrases to be used during a fire drill in the office.
phrases: If you see a fire, raise the alarm.
Walk calmly to your nearest fire exit.
Meet at the fire assembly point.

listening_challenge.question:
What colour are the fire exit signs?
Green.
listening_challenge.answer:
What colour are the fire exit signs?
Green.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Welcome back. Things are quite tense at Tip Top Trading today. Paul, the boss, mistakenly thinks Anna's been smoking on company premises and she's trying to explain herself.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: But, but…

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Frankly, I'm disappointed with you Anna. You're a hard worker but it doesn't mean you can go against company policy.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Anna, remember the phrases we've learnt about a misunderstanding!

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Oh yes. Paul, I think there's been a misunderstanding.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: A misunderstanding? How can you explain the smell of cigarette smoke? This is a 'no smoking' building.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Let me explain. I went down to the warehouse to speak to Mr Ingle and… well… someone else was smoking.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: What!? Someone was smoking in the warehouse? Golly gosh, that's highly dangerous. Who was it Anna?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Err… well… I can't really say. But I dealt with it and it won't happen again.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Yes, you dealt with it very well Anna but can you keep your secret about Mr Ingle safe?

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Thank you Anna and sorry about the misunderstanding. Would you like a biscuit? Now I really think it's time we had a review of our health and safety procedures.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Denise, could you gather everyone round in the meeting room please.

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: (On phone) I'll have to call you back Marge. (Hangs up) Could you all gather in the meeting room please, Paul has something important to say.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: What is it Denise? Is it about my fantastic sales figures again, huh?

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: I doubt it Tom. It sounded urgent. I'd better bring some tea.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Thank you for joining me. Unfortunately, there has been an incident in the warehouse. Someone has been smoking and I'm not happy, so I thought I would remind you of our health and safety procedures.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Not this again!

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Your safety is our responsibility. But to keep safe we must follow some simple rules. Denise, what's the first one?

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: (Slurps tea) If you see a fire, raise the alarm – oh and call the fire service.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Yeah, you love seeing those firemen, don't you, Denise!

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Shhh Tom. Maybe you could tell us the other rule?

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Oh yeah right. If you hear the fire alarm, get out quick.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Not exactly Tom. I think we should walk calmly to our nearest fire exit, following the green signs, go outside and meet at the fire assembly point.

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Yes, and I will take a register of who is here, using my red pen (slurps tea).

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Do you mind not slurping Denise?

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: This is thirsty work.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Hmm. Now is everyone clear about what to do if there is a fire alarm?

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: It's usually a false alarm anyway.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: That's not the point. Now Anna, what about smoking?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: No smoking on company premises. But it wasn't me, it was Mr Ingle.

transcript.speaker: All
transcript.text: Mr Ingle!

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: I see, so it was Mr Ingle smoking in the warehouse. You should have told me Anna.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Sorry!

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Right, I'm going to have to look into this. Back to work everyone… oh and take a biscuit with you.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text:
So Anna's let the cat out of the bag – Mr Ingle won't be pleased – but at least she now knows what do if a fire breaks out. Here are some of the phrases we've heard today, that can be used in an emergency:
If you see a fire, raise the alarm.
Walk calmly to your nearest fire exit.
Meet at the fire assembly point.
No smoking on company premises.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Sorry to interrupt Paul… but the fire alarm's going off!

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Don't panic anyone. Everything will be OK. (On phone) Jane, I'll have to call you back… yes, a bit of a panic. Bye. Quick, where's my red pen?

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Uh-oh. Those emergency phrases might come in useful sooner than you think. Is this going to be the end of Tip Top Trading, will it really go up in smoke? Find out next time. Bye.
